key_insight: LLM-derived language representations complemented cognitive scores and traditional linguistic features, with combined models improving prediction of APOE4 carrier status and amyloid-β burden.
clinical_relevance: Picture-description language may support research toward non-invasive early risk screening, but these findings do not establish clinical diagnostic utility.
method: Analyzed Cookie Theft picture descriptions from Hebrew- and English-speaking cohorts.
Compared pretrained LLM embeddings with cognitive test scores and theory-driven linguistic features.
Combined predictions using an any-positive ensemble across APOE4 and amyloid-β classification tasks.
evidence_signal: Across IRAP (N=134) and WRAP (N=1,541), LLM models achieved the highest constituent-model F1 in 5 of 8 APOE4/global amyloid-β tasks; the ensemble significantly outperformed all constituent models in all 8 tasks and 21 of 24 regional amyloid-β tasks.
watch_item: An any-positive ensemble may increase false positives; clinical use requires assessment of specificity, calibration, and external generalizability.
paper_title: LLM Representations Rival Traditional Predictors and Enhance Multimodal Prediction of APOE4 and Aβ-Burden
